blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — JG Summit Holdings Inc.’s net income attributable to equity holders of the parent fell 33 percent to P12.5 billion in the first nine months of 2026, as higher jet fuel costs and a weaker peso weighed on its airline business. On Friday, the Gokongwei-led conglomerate pointed said the peso’s depreciation increased foreign exchange translation losses on foreign-currency debt.
